stem.en: What does "commitment" mean?

options.en: a promise to give your time and effort
a short rest between two busy lessons
a prize for the best team of the year
a mistake that you make more than once

why.en: Commitment is a promise to give your time and effort, often for a long time.
why.uz: Commitment — vaqt va kuch sarflashga berilgan vaʼda, koʻpincha uzoq muddatga.
why.ru: Commitment — обещание отдавать своё время и силы, часто надолго.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Helping at the animal shelter is hard work, but it is very ___."

why.en: Work that gives you a good feeling is rewarding; reluctant describes a person, not work.
why.uz: Yaxshi his beradigan ish — rewarding (qoniqish beradigan). Reluctant ishni emas, odamni tasvirlaydi.
why.ru: Работа, которая приносит радость, — rewarding. Слово reluctant описывает человека, а не работу.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "Our school made a ___ to plant a tree for every new pupil."

why.en: After "made a" we need a noun: to make a commitment is to promise to do something.
why.uz: «made a» dan keyin ot kerak: make a commitment — biror ishni qilishga vaʼda bermoq.
why.ru: После «made a» нужно существительное: make a commitment — взять на себя обязательство.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Nobody asked Kamola to help; she ___ the initiative and called the shelter herself."

why.en: We say take the initiative: to act first, without waiting to be asked.
why.uz: Inglizchada take the initiative deyiladi: hech kim soʻramasdan birinchi boʻlib harakat qilmoq.
why.ru: По-английски говорят take the initiative: действовать первым, не дожидаясь просьбы.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Each family contributed ___ the new playground in our street."

why.en: The verb is contribute to something: each family helped to pay for the playground.
why.uz: Feʼl contribute to shaklida ishlatiladi: har bir oila maydonchaga hissa qoʻshgan.
why.ru: Глагол употребляется как contribute to: каждая семья внесла вклад в площадку.

stem.en: In "Bobur was reluctant to speak at the meeting", which word is closest in meaning to "reluctant"?

why.en: Reluctant means unwilling: Bobur could speak, but he did not want to.
why.uz: Reluctant — unwilling, yaʼni istamaydigan: Bobur gapira olardi, lekin xohlamadi.
why.ru: Reluctant значит unwilling, то есть не желающий: Бобур мог говорить, но не хотел.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Sardor has helped at the shelter every Sunday for three years, even in the coldest weeks of winter. His ___ is an example to the whole class."

why.en: Years of steady help show commitment; an initiative is a new plan, and Sardor started nothing new.
why.uz: Yillar davomida muntazam yordam — commitment (sodiqlik). Initiative — yangi reja, Sardor esa yangi narsa boshlamagan.
why.ru: Годы постоянной помощи — это commitment. Initiative — новый план, а Сардор ничего нового не начинал.

stem.en: Which sentence uses "rewarding" correctly?

options.en: Fixing the old bikes was rewarding.
She was rewarding to join the team.
He felt rewarding after the long walk.
I am rewarding to see you again.

why.en: Rewarding describes an activity that gives satisfaction, not how a person feels: "Fixing the old bikes was rewarding."
why.uz: Rewarding odamning holatini emas, qoniqish beradigan ishni tasvirlaydi: «Fixing the old bikes was rewarding.»
why.ru: Rewarding описывает занятие, а не чувства человека: «Fixing the old bikes was rewarding.»

stem.en: In "a new recycling initiative", what does "initiative" mean?

options.en: a new plan to deal with a problem
a person who leads a team

why.en: An initiative is a new plan to deal with a problem, here a plan for recycling.
why.uz: Initiative — tashabbus, yaʼni muammoni hal qilish uchun yangi reja; bu yerda chiqindini qayta ishlash rejasi.
why.ru: Initiative — инициатива, новый план для решения проблемы; здесь — план по переработке.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Many teenagers are ___ to volunteer because they think it will take too much of their free time."

why.en: After "are" we need an adjective, and the reason is a negative one: teenagers are reluctant, not willing.
why.uz: «are» dan keyin sifat kerak, sabab esa salbiy: oʻsmirlar reluctant, yaʼni istamaydi.
why.ru: После «are» нужно прилагательное, а причина отрицательная: подростки reluctant, то есть не хотят.

stem.en: What does "requirement" mean?

options.en: something that you must have or do
something you would like to try
a room where students take exams
a reason to feel proud of yourself

why.en: A requirement is something that you must have or do, for example a test score for a course.
why.uz: Requirement — talab, yaʼni albatta boʻlishi yoki bajarilishi kerak boʻlgan narsa.
why.ru: Requirement — требование: то, что обязательно нужно иметь или сделать.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Many students apply for a ___ because studying abroad is expensive."

why.en: Money that pays for study is a scholarship, and you apply for a scholarship.
why.uz: Oʻqish uchun beriladigan pul — scholarship (stipendiya); unga apply for bilan ariza beriladi.
why.ru: Деньги на учёбу — scholarship (стипендия); на неё подают заявку: apply for.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "Getting enough sleep before the exam should be your top ___."

why.en: After "your top" we need a noun: your top priority is the most important thing.
why.uz: «your top» dan keyin ot kerak: top priority — eng muhim ish.
why.ru: После «your top» нужно существительное: top priority — самое важное дело.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Before you apply, check that you ___ all the entry requirements."

why.en: We say meet a requirement: to have or do everything that is asked.
why.uz: Inglizchada meet a requirement deyiladi: talab qilingan hamma narsaga ega boʻlmoq.
why.ru: По-английски говорят meet a requirement: соответствовать требованию.

stem.en: In "After many tries, she eventually passed her driving test", which word is closest in meaning to "eventually"?

why.en: Eventually means finally, in the end after a long time: she passed after many tries.
why.uz: Eventually — finally, yaʼni koʻp urinishdan keyin oxir-oqibat.
why.ru: Eventually значит finally — в конце концов, после многих попыток.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "Laylo wants to win an international prize, open her own lab and teach at a top university. Her friends say she is very ___."

why.en: After "very" we need an adjective; someone with big plans for success is ambitious.
why.uz: «very» dan keyin sifat kerak: katta maqsadlari bor odam — ambitious.
why.ru: После «very» нужно прилагательное: человек с большими планами — ambitious.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Sevara won a scholarship ___ study medicine at a university in Samarkand."

why.en: A scholarship to do something: after it come to and a verb, here to study.
why.uz: Scholarship dan keyin to + feʼl keladi: scholarship to study — oʻqish uchun stipendiya.
why.ru: После scholarship идёт to + глагол: scholarship to study — стипендия на учёбу.

stem.en: Which sentence uses "eventually" correctly?

options.en: We got lost, but eventually found it.
I eventually my homework every day.
She is very eventually at school.
The eventually bus was very late.

why.en: Eventually is an adverb that says something happened in the end: "We got lost, but eventually found it."
why.uz: Eventually — ravish, voqea oxir-oqibat roʻy berganini bildiradi: «We got lost, but eventually found it.»
why.ru: Eventually — наречие «в конце концов»: «We got lost, but eventually found it.»

stem.en: What does "ambitious" mean?

options.en: wanting very much to be successful
happy with what you already have

why.en: An ambitious person wants very much to be successful and works hard for it.
why.uz: Ambitious odam muvaffaqiyatga juda intiladi va buning uchun koʻp mehnat qiladi.
why.ru: Ambitious — человек, который очень хочет добиться успеха и много для этого работает.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Aziz liked three universities: one had the best teachers, one was near home, and one was cheap. In the end, low cost was his first ___."

why.en: The thing that matters most is your priority; Aziz chose by cost, so cost came first.
why.uz: Eng muhim narsa — priority. Aziz universitetni narxiga qarab tanladi, demak narx eng muhim edi.
why.ru: Самое важное — priority. Азиз выбирал по цене, значит, цена была для него главным.

stem.en: What does "income" mean?

options.en: money that you get from work
a list of jobs in a newspaper
the time when a shop opens
a place where workers eat lunch

why.en: Income is the money that you get from work, for example your pay each month.
why.uz: Income — daromad, yaʼni ishdan oladigan pulingiz.
why.ru: Income — доход, то есть деньги, которые получаешь за работу.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Looking after my little brother after school is my ___."

why.en: A duty that you must do is a responsibility; after "my" we need a noun.
why.uz: Bajarishingiz shart boʻlgan vazifa — responsibility (masʼuliyat); «my» dan keyin ot kerak.
why.ru: Обязанность — responsibility; после «my» нужно существительное.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "The new timetable gives workers more ___, so they can start later on Mondays."

why.en: After "gives workers more" we need a noun: flexibility, the chance to change your hours.
why.uz: «gives workers more» dan keyin ot kerak: flexibility — moslashuvchanlik.
why.ru: После «gives workers more» нужно существительное: flexibility — гибкость.

stem.en: Choose the word: "A good team leader is ready to ___ responsibility for the team's mistakes."

why.en: We say take responsibility for something: to accept that it is your duty.
why.uz: Inglizchada take responsibility for deyiladi: masʼuliyatni oʻz zimmasiga olmoq.
why.ru: По-английски говорят take responsibility for: брать на себя ответственность.

stem.en: Choose the word: "The workers negotiated ___ the owner for two more days off."

why.en: We negotiate with a person: the workers talked with the owner to agree.
why.uz: Negotiate with — kimdir bilan muzokara qilmoq: ishchilar egasi bilan kelishdi.
why.ru: Negotiate with — договариваться с кем-то: рабочие договорились с владельцем.

stem.en: In "a flexible timetable", which word is closest in meaning to "flexible"?

why.en: A flexible timetable can change to suit you, so it is adaptable; strict means the opposite.
why.uz: Flexible jadval sizga moslab oʻzgaradi, yaʼni adaptable; strict esa aksincha.
why.ru: Гибкое расписание можно менять под себя, то есть adaptable; strict — наоборот.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Dilshod promised to water our plants while we were away, and he did it every single day without a reminder. He is very ___."

why.en: Someone who keeps every promise can be trusted, so Dilshod is reliable, not flexible.
why.uz: Har bir vaʼdasini bajargan odamga ishonish mumkin: Dilshod reliable, flexible emas.
why.ru: Тот, кто выполняет каждое обещание, надёжен: Дилшод reliable, а не flexible.

stem.en: Which sentence uses "income" correctly?

options.en: Her income is higher than last year.
He incomes a lot of money each week.
We income at the office at nine.
The income was very kind to us.

why.en: Income is a noun for money you get, not a verb or a person: "Her income is higher than last year."
why.uz: Income — ot (olinadigan pul), feʼl ham, odam ham emas: «Her income is higher than last year.»
why.ru: Income — существительное (получаемые деньги), не глагол и не человек: «Her income is higher than last year.»

stem.en: What does "negotiate" mean?

options.en: to talk in order to agree on something
to refuse to listen to anyone
to leave a job without giving a reason

why.en: To negotiate is to talk in order to agree, for example on pay or hours.
why.uz: Negotiate — kelishish uchun gaplashmoq, masalan, maosh yoki ish soatlari haqida.
why.ru: Negotiate — обсуждать, чтобы договориться, например о зарплате или часах работы.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "The bus to our village is so ___ that people are often late for work."

why.en: People are often late, so the bus cannot be trusted: it is unreliable.
why.uz: Odamlar koʻp kechikadi, demak avtobusga ishonib boʻlmaydi: u unreliable (ishonchsiz).
why.ru: Люди часто опаздывают, значит, на автобус нельзя положиться: он unreliable (ненадёжный).

stem.en: What does "conclusion" mean?

options.en: what you decide after studying the facts
the first page of a long report
a question you ask your teacher in class

why.en: A conclusion is what you decide after studying the facts, usually at the end of a project.
why.uz: Conclusion — xulosa, yaʼni faktlarni oʻrganib chiqarilgan qaror.
why.ru: Conclusion — вывод: решение, к которому приходишь, изучив факты.

stem.en: Choose the word: "The teacher found clear ___ that someone had copied the homework."

why.en: Facts that show something is true are evidence: the teacher found clear evidence of copying.
why.uz: Biror narsa toʻgʻriligini koʻrsatadigan faktlar — evidence: oʻqituvchi koʻchirilganiga dalil topdi.
why.ru: Факты, которые показывают, что что-то верно, — evidence: учитель нашёл явные доказательства.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "Aziz made a bold ___: our class would win the quiz."

why.en: After "made a bold" we need a noun: a prediction is what you say will happen.
why.uz: «made a bold» dan keyin ot kerak: prediction — bashorat.
why.ru: После «made a bold» нужно существительное: prediction — предсказание.

stem.en: Choose the word: "After a long discussion, the class ___ to the conclusion that the test had been too hard."

why.en: We say come to a conclusion: to decide something after thinking about the facts.
why.uz: Inglizchada come to a conclusion deyiladi: faktlarni oʻylab, xulosaga kelmoq.
why.ru: По-английски говорят come to a conclusion: прийти к выводу.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "The ___ into the broken window took two days."

why.en: After "The" we need a noun for a process that can take days: the investigation.
why.uz: «The» dan keyin jarayonni bildiruvchi ot kerak: investigation — tekshiruv, u ikki kun davom etdi.
why.ru: После «The» нужно существительное-процесс: investigation — расследование, оно шло два дня.

stem.en: In "Your measurements must be accurate", which word is closest in meaning to "accurate"?

why.en: Accurate measurements are correct in every detail, so they are exact.
why.uz: Accurate oʻlchovlar har bir tafsilotda toʻgʻri, yaʼni exact (aniq).
why.ru: Accurate — точные во всех деталях измерения, то есть exact.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "The thermometer said 25 degrees, but the room felt much colder. Later we found it was broken, so its reading was not ___."

why.en: A broken thermometer gives wrong numbers, so its reading was not accurate; "not inaccurate" would mean it was right.
why.uz: Buzuq termometr notoʻgʻri koʻrsatadi: reading was not accurate. «Not inaccurate» esa «toʻgʻri edi» degani.
why.ru: Сломанный термометр показывает неверно: reading was not accurate. «Not inaccurate» значило бы «верно».

stem.en: Which sentence uses "evidence" correctly?

options.en: We need more evidence before we decide.
She found three evidences in their lab.
The evidences shows he was there.
An evidence was left on the table.

why.en: Evidence is uncountable, never an evidence or evidences: "We need more evidence before we decide."
why.uz: Evidence sanalmaydigan ot, an evidence yoki evidences deyilmaydi: «We need more evidence before we decide.»
why.ru: Evidence — неисчисляемое, не an evidence и не evidences: «We need more evidence before we decide.»

stem.en: What does "investigate" mean?

options.en: to find out the facts about something
to repeat a test many times
to give a talk to a group
to build a model of a machine

why.en: To investigate is to find out the facts about something, for example with an experiment.
why.uz: Investigate — biror narsa haqidagi faktlarni aniqlamoq, masalan tajriba orqali.
why.ru: Investigate — выяснять факты о чём-то, например с помощью опыта.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Ravshan saw that bread went bad faster in the warm kitchen than in the cold room. To find out why, he decided to ___ it."

why.en: Finding out why something happens with an experiment is to investigate it.
why.uz: Tajriba bilan nima uchun shunday boʻlishini aniqlash — investigate (tekshirmoq).
why.ru: Выяснять с помощью опыта, почему что-то происходит, — это investigate.

stem.en: What does "headline" mean?

options.en: the title of a news story
the last line of a long letter
a phone number for the news
the name of a TV presenter

why.en: A headline is the title of a news story, printed in large letters above it.
why.uz: Headline — sarlavha, yaʼni yangilik ustida katta harflar bilan yozilgan nom.
why.ru: Headline — заголовок новости, крупными буквами над текстом.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Bad news can ___ very fast on social media."

why.en: After "can" we need a verb: news spreads when it reaches more and more people.
why.uz: «can» dan keyin feʼl kerak: spread — tarqalmoq, yaʼni tobora koʻp odamga yetib bormoq.
why.ru: После «can» нужен глагол: spread — распространяться, доходить до всё большего числа людей.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "The photo was changed to ___ readers about the size of the crowd."

why.en: After "to" we need the base form of the verb: to mislead readers is to make them believe something false.
why.uz: «to» dan keyin feʼlning asosiy shakli kerak: mislead — chalgʻitmoq, yolgʻonga ishontirmoq.
why.ru: После «to» нужна начальная форма глагола: mislead — вводить в заблуждение.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Someone ___ a rumour that the exam would be cancelled."

why.en: We say start a rumour: to be the first to tell a story that may not be true.
why.uz: Inglizchada start a rumour deyiladi: mish-mishni birinchi boʻlib tarqatmoq.
why.ru: По-английски говорят start a rumour: пустить слух.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Always check the source ___ a story before you share it."

why.en: We say the source of something: the place where a story comes from.
why.uz: The source of — biror narsaning manbasi: hikoya qayerdan kelgani.
why.ru: Говорят the source of: источник чего-либо, откуда пришла история.

stem.en: In "a misleading title", what does "misleading" mean?

why.en: Misleading means giving people the wrong idea, so they believe something false.
why.uz: Misleading — notoʻgʻri tasavvur beradigan, odamni yolgʻonga ishontiradigan.
why.ru: Misleading — создающий неверное впечатление, вводящий в заблуждение.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Nobody knew if the story about the bridge was true. People heard it from a friend of a friend. It was only a ___."

why.en: A story passed from person to person that may not be true is a rumour.
why.uz: Odamdan odamga oʻtadigan va rost boʻlmasligi mumkin boʻlgan gap — rumour (mish-mish).
why.ru: История, которая передаётся от человека к человеку и может быть неправдой, — rumour (слух).

stem.en: Which sentence uses "spread" correctly?

options.en: The story spread across the city.
The story spreaded across the city.

why.en: Spread is irregular: its past form is also spread, never spreaded: "The story spread across the city."
why.uz: Spread notoʻgʻri feʼl: oʻtgan zamonda ham spread, spreaded emas: «The story spread across the city.»
why.ru: Spread — неправильный глагол, в прошедшем тоже spread, не spreaded: «The story spread across the city.»

stem.en: What does "source" mean in "a news source"?

options.en: a short summary of the news
a photo at the top of a page

why.en: A source is where information comes from, for example a website or a person.
why.uz: Source — manba, yaʼni maʼlumot qayerdan kelishi.
why.ru: Source — источник, то есть откуда берётся информация.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "The advert said the course was free, but there were hidden costs. Many parents complained that it was ___."

why.en: After "it was" we need an adjective: the advert gave a false idea, so it was misleading.
why.uz: «it was» dan keyin sifat kerak: reklama yolgʻon tasavvur berdi, demak u misleading edi.
why.ru: После «it was» нужно прилагательное: реклама создала ложное впечатление — misleading.

stem.en: What does "resident" mean?

options.en: a person who lives in a place
a person who visits for a day

why.en: A resident is a person who lives in a place, not a visitor.
why.uz: Resident — biror joyda yashovchi odam, mehmon emas.
why.ru: Resident — житель, человек, который живёт в каком-то месте, а не гость.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Parks are especially important in ___ areas, where most people live in flats."

why.en: Areas of a town or city are urban areas; this adjective goes before "areas".
why.uz: Shahar hududlari — urban areas; bu sifat «areas» oldidan keladi.
why.ru: Городские районы — urban areas; это прилагательное стоит перед «areas».

stem.en: Choose the right form: "Regular ___ keeps the park clean and safe."

why.en: After "Regular" we need a noun: maintenance is the work of keeping something in good condition.
why.uz: «Regular» dan keyin ot kerak: maintenance — parvarish, yaxshi holatda saqlash ishi.
why.ru: После «Regular» нужно существительное: maintenance — уход, поддержание в порядке.

stem.en: Choose the word: "Everyone in the street will ___ from the new park."

why.en: We say benefit from something: to get a good effect from it.
why.uz: Benefit from — biror narsadan foyda koʻrmoq.
why.ru: Benefit from — получать пользу от чего-то.

stem.en: Choose the word: "We sat ___ the shade of the old walnut tree."

why.en: We say in the shade: inside the cool area that the tree covers.
why.uz: In the shade deyiladi: daraxt soyasining ichida.
why.ru: Говорят in the shade: в тени, под деревом.

stem.en: In "Residents complained about the noise", which word is closest in meaning to "residents"?

why.en: Residents are the people who live in a place, so they are its inhabitants.
why.uz: Residents — oʻsha joyda yashovchilar, yaʼni inhabitants.
why.ru: Residents — те, кто живёт в этом месте, то есть inhabitants (жители).

stem.en: Choose the word: "Nobody waters the trees or repairs the benches in the old park any more. If the city does not ___ it, the park will soon be lost."

why.en: Keeping a park in good condition by watering and repairing is to maintain it.
why.uz: Bogʻni sugʻorib, taʼmirlab yaxshi holatda saqlash — maintain.
why.ru: Поддерживать парк в порядке, поливая и ремонтируя, — это maintain.

stem.en: Which sentence uses "shade" correctly?

options.en: It is cooler here in the shade.
My shade follows me when I walk.
At noon my shade is very short.
Look at my shade on the wall!

why.en: Shade is a cool place out of the sun; your dark shape is a shadow: "It is cooler here in the shade."
why.uz: Shade — quyoshsiz salqin joy, tanangiz aksi esa shadow: «It is cooler here in the shade.»
why.ru: Shade — место без солнца, а силуэт тела — shadow: «It is cooler here in the shade.»

stem.en: What does "benefit" mean?

options.en: a good effect or an advantage
a problem that is hard to solve
a cost that you have to pay
a rule made by the city

why.en: A benefit is a good effect or an advantage that something gives you.
why.uz: Benefit — foyda, yaʼni biror narsaning yaxshi taʼsiri.
why.ru: Benefit — польза, хороший результат или преимущество.

stem.en: Choose the right form: "Planting trees along the road was ___ for everyone: the air became cleaner and the street quieter."

why.en: After "was" we need an adjective: beneficial means good for someone.
why.uz: «was» dan keyin sifat kerak: beneficial — foydali.
why.ru: После «was» нужно прилагательное: beneficial — полезный.
